extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, parties, and representatives participating in contested proceedings (interferences, contested cases, and PTAB trials) before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evidentiary rules governing motions, timing, discovery, testimony, exhibits, oral argument, sanctions, arbitration, judgment, and interference practice before the Board. Applies to parties and counsel conducting contested cases and patent interferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission by failure to deny
rubrics_metrics.description: Any material fact not specifically denied shall be considered admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denials must be specific; failure to specifically deny a material fact will cause that fact to be treated as admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions must contain all arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: All arguments for the relief requested in a motion must be made in the motion. A reply may only respond to arguments raised in the corresponding opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument omitted from the motion cannot later be introduced in replies; replies are limited to addressing opponent's arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default filing times for motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Default times: an opposition is due 30 days after service of the motion; a reply is due 30 days after service of the opposition; a responsive motion is due 30 days after service of the motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may set a different schedule; these are the default timing rules for non-miscellaneous motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous motions — consultation and authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: If no time for filing a specific miscellaneous motion is provided, the opposing party must be consulted prior to filing and, if an opposing party plans to oppose the miscellaneous motion, the movant may not file the motion without Board authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization ordinarily obtained by telephone conference including the Board and every other party. Delay in seeking relief may justify denial of the motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous motions — default times
rubrics_metrics.description: An opposition to a miscellaneous motion is due five business days after service of the motion; a reply to a miscellaneous motion opposition is due three business days after service of the opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An opposition may not be filed without Board authorization when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits must accompany first citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each exhibit must be filed and served with the first paper in which it is cited except as the Board may otherwise order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board orders otherwise, follow Board instructions; otherwise do not rely on later service of exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument — timing and request
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request an oral argument on an issue raised in a paper within five business days of the filing of the paper. The request must be filed as a separate paper and must specify the issues to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely, separate requests that clearly identify issues are required to preserve the right to oral argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument — copies for panel
rubrics_metrics.description: If an oral argument is set for a panel, the movant on any issue to be argued must provide three working copies of the motion, the opposition, and the reply. Each party is responsible for providing three working copies of its exhibits relating to the motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide requested hard copies in advance to facilitate panel review at argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument — time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for oral argument is granted, each party will have a total of 20 minutes to present its arguments, including any time for rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time is per party total; plan presentation and rebuttal within the 20-minute allotment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrative exhibits for oral argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrative exhibits must be served at least five business days before the oral argument and filed no later than the time of the oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve demonstratives early so opponents and the Board have time to review; late demonstratives may be disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument transcription
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board encourages transcription service use; if such service is to be used, the Board must be notified in advance and a transcript must be filed with the Board promptly after the oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify the Board in advance to ensure facilities and file transcript promptly to preserve the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on motions — Board discretion and order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may take up motions for decisions in any order, may grant, deny, or dismiss any motion, and may take such other action appropriate to secure the just, speedy, and inexpensive determination of the proceeding. A decision on a motion may include deferral of action on an issue until a later point in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect flexible Board management; motions need not be decided in filing order and may be deferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory decisions and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision on motions without a judgment is not final for the purposes of judicial review. A panel decision on an issue will govern further proceedings in the contested case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only decisions with judgment are final for judicial review; panel rulings control subsequent case activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration — Board authorization conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may resort to binding arbitration, but the Board will not authorize arbitration unless it is conducted under Title 9, the parties notify the Board in writing, the agreement is in writing, specifies the issues, names the arbitrator or provides a 30-day selection date, and provides that the arbitrator’s award is binding and judgment thereon can be entered by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if arbitration occurs, the Board remains able to independently determine patentability, jurisdiction, and Office practice; file copies of agreements and meet Board filing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration — procedural filing and effect of award
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the agreement must be filed within 20 days after execution; the arbitration completed within the time the Board sets; the award must be binding, in writing, state clearly each issue and disposition, and be filed within 20 days of the award. Once the award is filed, parties may not act inconsistent with the award and the Board may enter judgment if the award is dispositive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict filing and substance requirements must be met for the Board to consider and give effect to an arbitration award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment — estoppel within the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: A judgment disposes of all issues that were, or by motion could have properly been, raised and decided. A losing party who could have properly moved for relief on an issue, but did not so move, may not take action in the Office after the judgment that is inconsistent with that party’s failure to move, except where the party was awarded a favorable judgment on the contested subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to raise issues by motion may result in estoppel; judgment has broad preclusive effect within the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final disposal of a claim by adverse judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: An adverse judgment against a claim is a final action of the Office requiring no further action by the Office to dispose of the claim permanently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An adverse judgment ends Office proceedings on that claim absent successful rehearing or appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for adverse judgment by a party
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may at any time in the proceeding request judgment against itself; actions construed to be such a request include abandonment of an involved application, cancellation or disclaiming of a claim, concession of priority or unpatentability, or abandonment of the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties can voluntarily seek an adverse judgment via explicit actions listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing of a judgment — timing and burden
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with the judgment may file a request for rehearing within 30 days of the entry of the judgment. The request must specifically identify all matters the party believes to have been misapprehended or overlooked, and the place where the matter was previously addressed in a motion, opposition, or reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearing burden lies on the requester to identify specific errors and pinpoint where the issues were previously raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions — grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may impose a sanction against a party for misconduct, including failure to comply with an applicable rule or order; advancing a misleading or frivolous request for relief or argument; or engaging in dilatory tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misconduct covering procedural noncompliance, frivolous positions, and delay tactics may trigger sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions — remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions include holding certain facts established; expunging or precluding filing a paper; precluding a party from presenting or contesting a particular issue; precluding discovery; excluding evidence; awarding compensatory expenses including attorney fees; requiring terminal disclaimer of patent term; or entering judgment in the contested case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies are broad and may affect evidence, filings, monetary awards, and even substantive patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations to examiner following judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The judgment may include a recommendation for further action by the examiner or by the Director. If the Board recommends rejection of a claim of an involved application, the examiner must enter and maintain the recommended rejection unless an amendment or showing of facts not previously of record is filed which, in the opinion of the examiner, overcomes the recommended rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner generally must follow Board recommendations unless overcome by new amendment or facts not previously of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited discovery — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A party is not entitled to discovery except as authorized in this subpart. The parties may agree to discovery among themselves at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery is the exception, not the default; seek Board authorization or mutual agreement for additional discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic discovery — required disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 21 days of a request by an opposing party, a party must serve a legible copy of every requested patent, patent application, literature reference, and test standard mentioned in the specification of the party's involved patent or application, or application upon which the party will rely for benefit; if in another language, a translation if available; and file with the Board a notice (without copies) of service of the requested materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to automatic discovery requests and provide translations when available; separately notify the Board of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits cited in motions or testimony must be served
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless previously served, or the Board orders otherwise, any exhibit cited in a motion or in testimony must be served with the citing motion or testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on late exhibit service; serve exhibits concurrently with the paper that cites them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional discovery — interests of justice standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request additional discovery by showing such discovery is in the interests of justice. The Board may specify conditions for additional discovery. When appropriate, production of documents and things may be obtained during cross-examination or authorized testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for extra discovery must articulate why discovery is necessary and meet the interests-of-justice standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of the Federal Rules of Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, the Federal Rules of Evidence shall apply to contested cases. Portions relating to criminal proceedings, juries, and other matters not relevant to proceedings under this subpart shall not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat evidentiary issues under the Federal Rules except where explicitly excluded by the subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility — compliance with procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that is not taken, sought, or filed in accordance with this subpart shall not be admissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the subpart's procedures for taking, seeking, and filing evidence to preserve admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office records admissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification is not necessary as a condition to admissibility when the evidence to be submitted is a record of the Office to which all parties have access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records of the Office accessible to all parties are admissible without separate certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of evidence — exhibit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence consists of affidavits, transcripts of depositions, documents, and things. All evidence must be submitted in the form of an exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Package testimony and documents as exhibits per Board requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations for non-English documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party relies on a document or is required to produce a document in a language other than English, a translation of the document into English and an affidavit attesting to the accuracy of the translation must be filed with the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide certified translations and an accuracy affidavit when submitting non-English materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit labeling and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Each exhibit must have an exhibit label with a unique number in a range assigned by the Board, the names of the parties, and the proceeding number in the specified format (e.g., 'JONES EXHIBIT 2001; Jones v. Smith; Contested Case 104,999'). When the exhibit is a paper, each page must be uniquely numbered in sequence and the exhibit label must be affixed to the lower right corner of the first page without obscuring information (or affixed to a duplicate first page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the precise label format and page numbering rules to ensure exhibits are properly identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit list maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party must maintain an exhibit list with the exhibit number and a brief description of each exhibit. If the exhibit is not filed, the exhibit list should note that fact. The Board may require the filing of a current exhibit list prior to acting on a motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep exhibit lists current and accurate; be ready to file up-to-date lists on the Board's request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition objections and cure
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections to deposition evidence must be made during the deposition. Evidence to cure the objection must be provided during the deposition unless the parties to the deposition stipulate otherwise on the deposition record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise objections on the record during deposition to preserve them and provide any curative evidence as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections to non-deposition evidence — timing and supplemental response
rubrics_metrics.description: For evidence other than deposition evidence, any objection must be served within five business days of service of the evidence. The party relying on evidence for which an objection is timely served may respond by serving supplemental evidence within ten business days of service of the objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely file objections and be prepared to serve supplemental evidence within the specified ten-business-day window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to exclude and motion in limine
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to exclude must be filed to preserve any objection; the motion must identify the objections in the record in order and must explain the objections. A party may file a miscellaneous motion in limine for a ruling on the admissibility of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use motions to exclude or in limine to seek advance rulings on admissibility and to preserve objections for the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization to compel testimony or production
rubrics_metrics.description: A party seeking to compel testimony or production must file a miscellaneous motion for authorization describing the general relevance and, for testimony, identify the witness by name or title; for documents or things, describe the general nature of the document or thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear relevance statement and identification to obtain Board authorization to compel discovery or testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling testimony/production outside the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: For testimony or production sought outside the U.S., the motion must identify the foreign country, explain why the witness or documents can be compelled there (including procedures to be used and an estimated time to obtain them), and demonstrate reasonable efforts to secure agreement of the witness/entity to provide testimony/production in the U.S., including offering to pay expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show concrete steps taken to obtain cooperation and explain legal/ practical bases for compelling foreign evidence; provide time estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of direct testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct testimony must be submitted in the form of an affidavit except when the testimony is compelled under 35 U.S.C. 24, in which case it may be in the form of a deposition transcript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use affidavits for direct testimony unless a statutory compulsion allows deposition transcript form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and place for testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncompelled direct testimony may be taken at any time; otherwise, testimony may only be taken during such time period as the Board may authorize. Authorized testimony within the United States may be taken before any disinterested official authorized to administer oaths at that location; testimony outside the United States may only be taken as the Board specifically directs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain Board authorization for testimony timing and comply with location/oath requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of deposition — content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of the deposition must be filed at least two business days before a deposition. The notice limits the scope of the testimony and must list the time and place, the name and address of the witness, a list of exhibits to be relied upon during the deposition, and a general description of the scope and nature of the testimony to be elicited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full logistical and scope information in deposition notices to avoid waiver of objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement or Board conference to set deposition time/place
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to taking testimony, all parties must agree on the time and place. If the parties cannot agree, the party seeking the testimony must initiate a conference with the Board to set a time and place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempt to reach agreement first; if not possible, promptly request Board conference to set deposition schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination timing and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-examination should ordinarily take place after any supplemental evidence relating to the direct testimony has been filed and more than a week before the filing date for any paper in which the cross-examination testimony is expected to be used. A party requesting cross-examination testimony of more than one witness may choose the order in which witnesses are to be cross-examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule cross-examination to allow the opposing party time to incorporate testimony into filings; specify order when multiple witnesses involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to quash — preservation of notice defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Objection to a defect in the deposition notice is waived unless a miscellaneous motion to quash is promptly filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly move to quash to preserve notice-based objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition in a foreign language
rubrics_metrics.description: If an interpreter will be used during the deposition, the party calling the witness must initiate a conference with the Board at least five business days before the deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for interpreter logistics and notify the Board early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of taking testimony — formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each witness must be duly sworn by an authorized officer; testimony shall be taken in answer to interrogatories with questions and answers recorded in regular order; exhibits relied upon must be numbered according to the contested-case numbering scheme and, if not previously served, be served at the deposition; objections made at time of deposition are to be noted on the record and evidence taken subject to a ruling on the objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe oath, recording, exhibit numbering, and on-the-record objection practices to preserve the evidentiary record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition transcript certification and signing
rubrics_metrics.description: When the testimony has been transcribed, the witness shall read and sign (in the form of an affidavit) the transcript unless parties otherwise agree, waive reading/signature on the record, or the witness refuses. The officer shall prepare a certified transcript by attaching a certificate stating specified matters (e.g., witness sworn, true record, who recorded, presence of opponents, place/dates, officer has no disqualifying interest, and circumstances if witness refuses to sign). The officer must promptly provide a copy to all parties and the proponent must file the original as an exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure certified transcript and required certificate accompany filed deposition exhibit; provide copies to parties quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of deposition objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Any objection to the content, form, or manner of taking the deposition, including the qualifications of the officer, is waived unless made on the record during the deposition and preserved in a timely filed miscellaneous motion to exclude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make objections on the record during the deposition and follow up with a timely motion to exclude to avoid waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs of testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as the Board may order or the parties may agree in writing, the proponent of the testimony shall bear all costs associated with the testimony, including the reasonable costs associated with making the witness available for cross-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for testimony costs unless the Board orders otherwise or parties agree to different allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert testimony — underlying data required
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert testimony that does not disclose the underlying facts or data on which the opinion is based is entitled to little or no weight. Testimony on United States patent law will not be admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide underlying data and methodology for expert opinions; do not offer expert testimony about U.S. patent law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit requirements for technical tests and data
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party relies on a technical test or data from such a test, the party must provide an affidavit explaining: (1) why the test or data is being used, (2) how the test was performed and the data was generated, (3) how the data is used to determine a value, (4) how the test is regarded in the relevant art, and (5) any other information necessary for the Board to evaluate the test and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a detailed affidavit addressing rationale, procedures, data generation, use of data, art acceptance, and other evaluative information to support reliance on technical tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference existence standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An interference exists if the subject matter of a claim of one party would, if prior art, have anticipated or rendered obvious the subject matter of a claim of the opposing party and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interference requires mutual potential anticipation or obviousness between parties' claims when treated as prior art to one another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting an interference — applicant requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may suggest an interference. The suggestion must: (1) provide sufficient information to identify the application or patent, (2) identify all claims the applicant believes interfere, propose one or more counts, and show how the claims correspond to one or more counts, (3) for each count provide a claim chart comparing at least one claim of each party corresponding to the count and show why the claims interfere, (4) explain in detail why the applicant will prevail on priority, (5) if a claim has been added or amended to provoke the interference provide a claim chart showing the written description for each such claim, and (6) for each constructive reduction to practice for which the applicant wishes to be accorded benefit provide a chart showing where the disclosure provides a constructive reduction to practice within the scope of the interfering subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A suggestion to declare an interference must be supported with claim charts, priority analysis, written-description charts for provocative claims, and benefit charts for constructive reductions to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee and examiner roles in provocation of interference
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee cannot suggest an interference but may alert the examiner of an application claiming interfering subject matter. An examiner may require an applicant to add a claim to provoke an interference; failure to satisfy a requirement within a period (not less than one month) set by the examiner will operate as a concession of priority. The proposed claim must be patentable to the applicant and drawn to patentable subject matter claimed by another applicant or patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners can force claim additions to provoke interferences; applicants must timely comply or risk concession of priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to show priority when earlier benefit exists
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant's earliest constructive reduction to practice is later than the apparent earliest constructive reduction to practice for a patent or published application claiming interfering subject matter, the applicant must show why it would prevail on priority. If the applicant fails to show priority, an administrative patent judge may nevertheless declare an interference to place the applicant under an order to show cause why judgment should not be entered; new evidence in support of priority will not be admitted except on a showing of good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants facing earlier-accorded benefit must proactively demonstrate entitlement to priority and prepare good-cause showings for any late evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of a priority showing when discovery/testimony needed
rubrics_metrics.description: A showing of priority is not sufficient unless it would, if unrebutted, support a determination of priority in favor of the party making the showing. When testimony or production necessary to show priority is not available without authorization under §§ 41.150(c) or 41.156(a), the showing shall include any necessary interrogatory, request for admission, request for production, or deposition request, and a detailed proffer of what the response would be expected to be and an explanation of the relevance of the response to the question of priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When priority hinges on authorized discovery, include the precise discovery requests and detailed proffers explaining expected responses and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority statement content
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may not submit evidence of its priority in addition to its accorded benefit unless it files a statement setting forth all bases on which the party intends to establish its entitlement to judgment on priority. The priority statement must: (i) state the date and location of the party’s earliest corroborated conception, (ii) state the date and location of the party’s earliest corroborated actual reduction to practice, (iii) state the earliest corroborated date on which the party’s diligence began, and (iv) provide a copy of the earliest document upon which the party will rely to show conception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File complete priority statements with corroborated dates, locations, diligence onset, and supporting documentary evidence to avoid default judgment against a junior party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file priority statement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a junior party fails to file a priority statement overcoming a senior party’s accorded benefit, judgment shall be entered against the junior party absent a showing of good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Junior parties must timely and adequately file priority statements or risk automatic adverse judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ownership consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative patent judge may decline to declare, or if already declared the Board may issue judgment in, an interference between an application and another application or patent that are commonly owned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common ownership can be a basis for declining or terminating an interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions — priority and evidentiary standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are presumed to have invented interfering subject matter in the order of the dates of their accorded benefit for each count. If two parties are accorded the same earliest date, neither is entitled to a presumption. Priority may be proved by a preponderance of the evidence except a party must prove priority by clear and convincing evidence if the date of its earliest constructive reduction to practice is after the issue date of an involved patent or the publication date under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) of an involved application or patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accorded benefit dates drive presumptions; higher clear-and-convincing standard applies when the claimed earliest date is after involved patent issue or application publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions — claim correspondence and cross-applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims of a party corresponding to the count are presumed to stand or fall together; to challenge this presumption a party must file a timely substantive motion to have a corresponding claim designated as not corresponding. A claim corresponds to a count if the subject matter of the count, treated as prior art to the claim, would have anticipated or rendered obvious the subject matter of the claim. When a motion for judgment of unpatentability against an opponent’s claim on the basis of prior art is granted, each of the movant’s claims corresponding to the same count will be presumed to be unpatentable in view of the same prior art unless the movant in its motion rebuts this presumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use substantive motions to challenge claim-grouping presumptions; expect cross-applicability of prior-art rulings across corresponding claims unless rebutted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and sufficiency of substantive motions in interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: In an interference, substantive motions must: (1) raise a threshold issue, (2) seek to change the scope of the definition of the interfering subject matter or the correspondence of claims to the count, (3) seek to change the benefit accorded for the count, or (4) seek judgment on derivation or on priority. To be sufficient, a motion must provide a showing, supported with appropriate evidence, such that, if unrebutted, it would justify the relief sought. The burden of proof is on the movant. A party moving to add or amend a claim must show the claim is patentable; a party moving to add or amend a count must show the count is patentable over prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive motions must be focused on specified interference issues and include unrebutted-supporting evidence and patentability showings when adding claims or counts.
